title: Baby Dodds and the Mezzrow rhythm section at Nice
summary: Wilber praises Baby Dodds, the Price-Foster-Dodds rhythm section that unsettled the Armstrong All-Stars, and clarinet duets with Mezzrow.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Anything to say about Baby Dogs? We've got to have it in a minute.
Oh, yeah. Baby Dogs was marvelous.
God, I thought he was a great drummer.

And I loved playing with him, and he, the way he could make a press roll swing on the drums was just terrific. Yeah. Yeah. That rhythm section was, with, with Sam Price, Pop Foster, and Baby Dogs. That upset, uh, that upset the Armstrong All-Stars.
Uh, we, they all, they naturally would finish the concerts. It was a double bill with the two bands, and, because they were the big, big names, but we gave them an awful rough time.
Yeah, I heard Louie really liked to hear that, too. Yeah. He's really a little bit.

And, uh, Mes and I would play these clarinet duets and everything. Of course, Mes had a thing that he would do, which, what used to get me mad. And he always was having a little read trouble, and, and he would squeak, and he'd always give me a dirty look when he'd squeak. For the, gee, really? He wanted the people to think that I was, you know.
Oh, gee, that's funny. That's pretty good.
But we used to do, uh, all the things that, like, the weary blues, and really the blues, and the things that he'd recorded with Sidney, and I'd take Sidney.
